questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles per-task state on its pooled worker threads? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The pool has 4 core threads, 8 maximum threads and an `ArrayBlockingQueue` of 200. 4 tasks are running and a 5th arrives. What happens?
choices: A fifth thread is started immediately because the core threads are busy
The caller runs the task itself because the pool is at its core size
The task waits in the queue; extra threads are only started once the 200-slot queue is full
The task is rejected because only 4 threads are guaranteed

questions.prompt: Under a sustained overload, all 8 threads are busy and the queue holds 200 tasks. A request thread calls `trending(20)`. What is the most likely result?
choices: The call throws RejectedExecutionException to the request thread
The task is dropped and the returned future never completes
The oldest queued task is discarded to make room
The request thread executes `buildTrending` itself, which slows that caller and throttles new submissions

questions.prompt: `ranker.rank` throws a RuntimeException for one viewer. What does the caller of `personalized(...)` observe?
choices: A future that completes exceptionally; the pool thread itself keeps running
The exception propagates to the thread that called `personalized`
The pool thread terminates and is replaced by a new one
An empty list, because supplyAsync swallows exceptions
